description: JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprint database for scanner/bot detection. Built from baseline scans against the Quiet Room honeypot (local VLAN 47 + AWS public instance).

local.notes: Local scans have no SNI extension — JA4 prefix uses 'i' flag and has 1 fewer extension than AWS scans

aws.notes: AWS scans have SNI — JA4 prefix uses 'd' flag. Cipher and extension hashes remain stable across environments.

fields.cipher_hash: truncated SHA-256 of sorted cipher suite list
fields.ext_hash: truncated SHA-256 of sorted extension list

ja4_format_reference.key_insight: The cipher_hash and ext_hash (2nd and 3rd components) are stable across environments. The prefix changes based on SNI presence and ALPN negotiation. For environment-agnostic detection, match on cipher_hash + ext_hash.

fingerprints.behavior: One TLS handshake per HTTP request. Consistent fingerprint. Requests HTTP/2 via ALPN.
fingerprints.notes: Standard OpenSSL fingerprint. Also matches other OpenSSL-based CLI tools. JA3 changes between local/AWS due to SNI extension, but JA4 cipher/ext hashes remain stable.

fingerprints.behavior: One TLS handshake per request. GnuTLS offers 68 cipher suites — the largest of any tool tested. No ALPN.
fingerprints.notes: GnuTLS fingerprint with unusually large cipher suite list (68 including CAMELLIA, ARIA). Unique among common tools.

fingerprints.behavior: Same fingerprint for urllib, http.client, requests, httpx — all use Python ssl module. Smallest cipher set (17) of any tested tool.
fingerprints.notes: Python ssl.create_default_context() aggressively filters cipher suites. One of the most common bot/scraper fingerprints on the internet.

fingerprints.behavior: Primary probe with 71 ciphers, then ~55 cipher-enumeration probes across TLS 1.0/1.1/1.2/1.3/SSLv3. Each probe has a unique JA4 due to different cipher subsets. The burst of many unique JA4 prefixes (t10/t11/t12/t13/ts3) from one source is a dead giveaway.
detection_signals: 55+ unique JA4 fingerprints from single source within seconds
SSLv3 probes (ts3i*) — no legitimate modern client uses SSLv3
TLS 1.0 probes (t10i*) — extremely rare in modern traffic
Extension hash 99875426d20b shared across all TLS 1.2 cipher probes
fingerprints.notes: Trivially detectable: 55+ distinct JA4s in rapid succession, including SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 probes. The primary probe's 71-cipher suite count is also abnormally high.

fingerprints.behavior: Single consistent fingerprint across all 377 requests. 377 handshakes in ~3 seconds. No ALPN.
fingerprints.notes: Go crypto/tls fingerprint (25 ciphers, no ALPN). Shared by nuclei, gobuster, ffuf, subfinder, and other Go security tools. Different from WebFetch's Go fingerprint (13 ciphers) — nuclei uses an older Go TLS configuration.

fingerprints.behavior: 89 TLS sessions across 3 source IPs. Consistent fingerprint. All sessions to same domain. Go crypto/tls but with only 13 ciphers — a much more restricted set than nuclei's 25.
fingerprints.notes: Anthropic's WebFetch uses Go crypto/tls but with a modern, minimal cipher suite (13 ciphers including only TLS 1.3 and ECDHE suites). Distinct from nuclei/gobuster Go fingerprints which offer 25 ciphers including legacy suites. The cipher_hash f57a46bbacb6 is unique to this Go TLS configuration.

wild_scanner_fingerprints.description: JA4 fingerprints observed from wild internet scanners hitting the AWS honeypot within minutes of deployment

coordinated_nmap_scanner.behavior: 5 IPs performing identical nmap-style cipher enumeration within the same 2-minute window. Same cipher suites but randomized TLS extension ordering — active JA3 evasion. JA4 cipher hashes (ea0618708e31) remain consistent across the coordinated scan.
coordinated_nmap_scanner.notes: JA3 randomization detected: same cipher suites, randomized extensions. JA4's sorted hashing partially defeats this — cipher_hash ea0618708e31 is shared across many of these probes.

persistent_go_scanner.notes: Go crypto/tls with same cipher_hash as WebFetch (f57a46bbacb6) but from known scanner IPs. Demonstrates that Go's cipher_hash alone cannot distinguish legitimate from malicious Go clients — behavioral analysis needed.

misc_scanners.description: Various single-session probes from different IPs
misc_scanners.notes: Single-request probes. Cipher hash 8daaf6152771 appears across multiple IPs — likely a shared scanning framework.

detection_rules.description: Detection logic for Security Onion / Suricata / Arkime. JA4 inner hashes are preferred over full JA4 strings for environment-agnostic matching.

ja4_based.name: SCAN-JA4-NMAP-SSLV3
ja4_based.notes: SSLv3 ClientHello — no legitimate modern client uses SSLv3

ja4_based.name: SCAN-JA4-NMAP-TLS10
ja4_based.notes: TLS 1.0 ClientHello — very rare in modern traffic, usually cipher enumeration

ja4_based.name: SCAN-JA4-NUCLEI-GO
ja4_based.notes: Go crypto/tls with legacy cipher set (25 ciphers). Matches nuclei, gobuster, ffuf.

ja4_based.name: SCAN-JA4-WGET
ja4_based.notes: GnuTLS with 68 cipher suites — unique to wget and GnuTLS clients

ja4_based.name: SCAN-JA4-PYTHON-SSL
ja4_based.notes: Python ssl module (17 ciphers). Very common for bots, scrapers, and legitimate automation.
